title: Open projection routes and their canonical restrictions
statement: For a finite commutative coefficient ring A, a cartesian square (a,j',j,h) with both vertical arrows open immersions, and arbitrary K on the source of j and P on its target, the actual fixed-scalar maps openFirst and openSecond agree. Restricting either map by the pullback functor of j' and following by openUnitInv gives the independently constructed openSource. All maps are those of [def-sf-finite-projection-exchange-coordinates].

proof.text: Use the actual adjunction Dj_! ⊣ Lj^*, transported by leftDerivedUpperStarIsoMapDerivedCategory. The canonical openUnitInv is its inverse unit. The published mateEquiv_leftDerivedUpperStarOpenImmersionLowerShriekBaseChangeIso_inv gives the unit equation for beta. The adjunction projectionMap unit equation, transported through the same comparison, gives the unit equation for gamma. Cancelling the invertible units gives beta_restriction and gamma_restriction. These are proved private calculations, not additional assumptions.

Expand openFirst and openSecond. Apply the restriction equations, naturality of the unit and of the pullback tensor comparison, and bifunctoriality of tensorMap. For openSecond use tensor_square for the open square. Each restriction is exactly openSource. The common target is an extension-by-zero object; use the adjunction hom-equivalence and the invertible unit to deduce openFirst = openSecond from their equal restrictions.

theorem open_factor_routes
    {X' X B' B : Scheme.{u}} {a : X' ⟶ X} {j' : X' ⟶ B'}
    {j : X ⟶ B} {h : B' ⟶ B} [IsOpenImmersion j] [IsOpenImmersion j']
    (s : IsPullback a j' j h) (K : Dcat A X) (P : Dcat A B) :
    openFirst A s K P = openSecond A s K P ∧
    (pull A j').map (openFirst A s K P) ≫ openUnitInv A j' _ = openSource A s K P ∧
    (pull A j').map (openSecond A s K P) ≫ openUnitInv A j' _ = openSource A s K P
